title: Build a Content Calendar: Plan a Month of Posts in One Afternoon
excerpt: A simple, repeatable method for planning a month of content in one sitting — the exact framework we use with clients.

content.text: The hardest part of content marketing isn't writing. It's deciding what to write, then remembering to do it. A content calendar solves both.
Here's the exact process we use with clients. You can finish it in one afternoon, including the coffee break.
Step 1: List What Your Customers Ask
Write down every question customers have asked you in the last three months. These are your best post ideas, already proven by real interest.
A Nairobi logistics company built an entire month of content from one recurring question: how long does delivery actually take?
Step 2: Map Each Idea to a Goal

items: Awareness posts: teach something useful, no hard sell
Trust posts: behind the scenes, team, process
Conversion posts: offers, comparisons, case studies

content.text: A healthy month has mostly awareness, some trust, and one or two conversion posts.
Step 3: Assign One Slot Per Idea
Open your calendar tool and put one post in each slot. Many businesses use a simple pattern: Mondays for how-to content, Wednesdays for opinions, Fridays for news and updates.
Step 4: Write Titles and Keywords Now
Don't leave titles for later. A title written today forces you to commit to the angle. Add the target keyword next to it, so every post has a purpose beyond filling a slot.
Book two half-day sessions per month and write four posts per session. Batching beats one hour here and there, because your brain stays in writing mode.
You don't need a fancy tool. A Google Sheet with columns for date, title, keyword, status, and notes is enough to run a serious content engine.
One post per week, every week, beats five posts one month and silence the next. Readers and Google both reward rhythm.
Set the calendar once, follow it, and review every 30 days. That's the whole system.
A plan you follow is worth more than a perfect plan you abandon.
